text: The Bob Marley Museum is a tourist attraction in Kingston, Jamaica, dedicated to the reggae musician Bob Marley. Located at 56 Hope Road, Kingston, it was Bob Marley's former residence.[1] The property housed the Tuff Gong reggae record label, which was founded by The Wailers in 1970. In 1976, the building was the site of a failed assassination attempt on Bob Marley.[2] After his death, the property was converted into a museum in 1986 by his wife, Rita Marley.[3] The song "56 Hope Road" from the album In the Pursuit of Leisure by Sugar Ray featuring Shaggy is named in reference to the home.
